automation.label: Google Workspace
automation.mentionLabel: Only mail addressed directly to you (your address in To)
automation.starterPrompt: Google Workspace events just arrived — each line of the payload is one JSON event. Type `mail` is new Gmail: the author is the sender, content holds the subject and a text excerpt, and extra carries the message id, thread id, labels and attachment names (`gw mail read <id>` for the whole thing). Type `event` is a calendar event about to start: content holds the title, time and location, and extra carries the event id, calendar, attendees and any meeting link. Triage what arrived and act on it — `gw` is on your PATH for the whole of Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets and Contacts.

catalog.name: Google Workspace
catalog.description: Your Google mail, calendar, files and docs.
catalog.hint: One connection covers all six. Connect as YOUR ACCOUNT (a personal Gmail address or a single Workspace one) with an OAuth client you make in Google's console, or as a WHOLE COMPANY (a Workspace admin's service account with domain-wide delegation, where each card acts as one named person). The read-only setting is real, not cosmetic: it asks Google for the read-only scopes AND refuses every command that sends, edits, moves or deletes. Add the card again for a second account.

guide.scopes: read & write: `gmail.modify` `gmail.send` `calendar` `drive` `documents` `spreadsheets` `contacts` — read only: the `.readonly` form of each
steps: In `console.cloud.google.com`, create a project (or pick one), then under `APIs & Services` → `Library` enable `Gmail API`, `Google Calendar API`, `Google Drive API`, `Google Docs API`, `Google Sheets API` and `People API`.
YOUR ACCOUNT — `APIs & Services` → `OAuth consent screen`: user type `External`, add yourself as a test user, and add the scopes above.

YOUR ACCOUNT — on that same screen set the publishing status to `In production`. This one matters: a screen left in `Testing` hands out refresh tokens that STOP WORKING AFTER 7 DAYS, and the connection then dies for no visible reason. `In production` without Google's verification is fine for your own account — you click through an `unverified app` warning once.

YOUR ACCOUNT — `Credentials` → `Create credentials` → `OAuth client ID` → `Web application`, and add `https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground` as an authorized redirect URI. Copy the client ID and client secret.

YOUR ACCOUNT — open `developers.google.com/oauthplayground`, click the gear, tick `Use your own OAuth credentials` and paste the pair. Select the scopes above, `Authorize APIs`, approve, then `Exchange authorization code for tokens` and copy the REFRESH token. Paste all three here.
WHOLE COMPANY — `IAM & Admin` → `Service Accounts` → create one → `Keys` → `Add key` → `JSON`, and note the service account's numeric `Client ID`.

WHOLE COMPANY — in `admin.google.com` → `Security` → `Access and data control` → `API controls` → `Domain-wide delegation`, add that client ID with the full scope URLs (`https://www.googleapis.com/auth/` + each scope above). Paste the JSON key here and the address the agent should act as.

Prefer not to use the playground? Connect with the client ID and secret and run `gw auth login` in a chat — the agent walks you through approving in the sandbox's own browser and hands you the refresh token to paste.

fields.label: Google account
fields.hint: The address this connection acts as. In company mode it is the person the service account impersonates.

fields.label: Refresh token
fields.hint: Rotate this here when Google revokes it — a password change, six months idle, or a hundredth token on the same client all do that.

fields.label: Service account key (JSON)
fields.hint: The whole downloaded JSON file, pasted.
